audit.whatIsWrong: The full-layer chart disagreed with the content layer on all seven rows: full read Malzahar, Malzahar, Skill, Skill, Malzahar, Skill, Skill while win[] read Akali, Akali, Malzahar, Malzahar, Akali, Akali, Akali.
audit.why: win[] matches packet.levelChart exactly, and its shape is the right one — Akali presses at 1-2 before the silence exists, concedes 3-5, retakes it at 6. The full layer even had level 6 as Malzahar's, which contradicts its own spikes text.
audit.corrected: All seven phases[N].side realigned to win[N] as one group, with each phase why rewritten to its new owner.

audit.whatIsWrong: The spikes never mentioned the state that actually decides whether an all-in works.
audit.why: Void Shift gives him massive damage reduction AND crowd-control immunity whenever he hasn't recently taken damage, lingering briefly after he does. An Akali who opens her full combo into an intact Void Shift loses the trade she should have won — the fix is one Q of chip first, which is free.
audit.corrected: 'Strip Void Shift with a Q before you commit' written into the spikes, tradeGood, breakdown.carry, ahead and the loading screen.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three attribution errors: the silence was credited to 'Malefic Visions/Nether Grasp setup'; Void Swarm was called 'his passive'; and Void Shift was called a 'passive shield' whose Voidlings give 'passive stacks'.
audit.why: The silence is Call of the Void (Q), 900 range on a flat 6s. Void Swarm is W, an 8s summon, not the passive. Void Shift is the passive and it is damage reduction plus CC immunity, not a shield — the difference matters because your Q slow and every form of CC you have simply does not apply to him while it is up. The silence is the other half: a silenced Akali has no shroud, no flip and no exit, which is the real reason levels 3-5 are his.
audit.corrected: Every ability put back in its own slot, with the silence's 6s and the passive's condition stated where the advice depends on them.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns gave no numbers at all.
audit.why: Nether Grasp is 140s at rank 1 — the longest cooldown either champion has, and baiting it once buys more than two minutes. Call of the Void is a flat 6s, so the silence gaps are countable.
audit.corrected: Both numbers written in and used as the commit trigger in dosFull[0], dosFull[2], phases[4] and report[5].

audit.whatIsWrong: Malefic Visions' behaviour after you disengage was never mentioned.
audit.why: Flagged in missingInteractions (execute-threshold). It is a damage-over-time that keeps ticking once you have walked away, and if it kills you it passes to a nearby unit and refunds him mana — so the trade you think you won can still finish you. Track the number, not the bar.
audit.corrected: Written into phases[3].why, whys[3], breakdown.wave and mid.

notes: packet.suspectNames flagged 'Nether Grasp's' and 'Land Malefic Visions' as probable wrong names — both are FALSE POSITIVES; those are his real R and E. The genuine name errors were elsewhere and unflagged: spikes[0] credited the silence to 'Malefic Visions/Nether Grasp setup' when it is Call of the Void (Q); early called Void Swarm 'his passive' when Void Swarm is W and Void Shift is the passive; and mid told the reader to kill Voidlings 'to deny his passive scaling' and to avoid 'Malefic Visions' detonation radius', which is a single-target damage-over-time that spreads on the target's death, not a zone. Void Shift itself was described as a 'passive shield' — it is massive damage reduction plus crowd-control immunity, which means your Q slow does nothing to him while it holds, and one Q of chip strips it. That is now the central piece of advice. Full-layer chart disagreed with content on all seven rows, including a level 6 row that contradicted the page's own level 6 spike text.
